html:
The Twana are a Coast Salish people of Hood Canal, the long fjord on the west side of Puget Sound in Washington State. The Skokomish, "river people", were the largest of their villages and give their name to the present Skokomish Indian Tribe.

Like other Coast Salish peoples they lived from salmon, shellfish and cedar, in winter villages of plank houses. In 1855 they signed the Treaty of Point No Point with the United States and were moved to a reservation at the mouth of the Skokomish River. Their neighbours included the Nisqually to the south.
